title: Publish a ChatGPT canvas
metaTitle: Publish a ChatGPT canvas as a website · Aero
description: Put a page you made in ChatGPT online at its own address. Paste one prompt into the chat, or save the code as index.html and upload it.
answer: Copy one prompt from Aero into the ChatGPT chat where you made the page. ChatGPT sends the files to Aero and replies with the address. Or copy the code out of the canvas, save it as index.html and upload it.
needs: The ChatGPT chat where you made the page
An Aero account (free)

steps.name: Start a new site from a prompt
steps.text: In Aero, go to Sites, New site, and pick From Claude or ChatGPT.

steps.name: Copy the prompt
steps.text: Aero shows one prompt with your publish key in it. Press Copy prompt. The key only lets this prompt publish sites in your account. Treat it like a password.

steps.name: Paste it into your ChatGPT chat
steps.text: Go back to the chat where you made the page, paste the prompt and send it. ChatGPT sends the files to Aero and replies with the address.

steps.name: Open the site in Aero
steps.text: The page in Aero updates by itself when the site is live. Press Done to open its page: the address, a preview and its versions.

alt.p: Copy the code from the canvas into a text file and save it as index.html. Then go to New site, Upload HTML and drop the file in.

gets: A live site at an address like yourname.aeroapp.ai
A copy of your page. The canvas in ChatGPT doesn’t change
Every version kept, so you can go back
On the free plan the site stays live for 7 days
faq: Does my page stay in ChatGPT?
Yes. Aero publishes a copy at its own address. Your chat and the canvas don’t change.
How do I update the site?
Ask ChatGPT for the change in the same chat, then use the prompt again. Aero keeps every version.
Can I keep it private?
Add a password on Basic and up, so only people you give it to can open it.
How long does a free site stay live?
7 days. Paid plans keep it live; they start at $3 a month with a 7-day free trial.
Can I test it with people?
Yes. Start a new test and pick this site. You get a test link to send to anyone.

title: Publish a Lovable app
metaTitle: Publish a Lovable app on its own address · Aero
description: Aero publishes the built files of a Lovable app. Export the code, build it, drop the output folder in, and it’s live at an aeroapp.ai address.
answer: Aero has no Lovable integration. Get your project’s code out of Lovable, build it into static files, then drop the folder or a zip of it into Aero. Or open the project in a coding agent and paste Aero’s publish prompt.
needs: Your project’s code, out of Lovable
Node.js on your computer, to build it (or a coding agent that does it for you)
An Aero account (free)

steps.name: Get the code out of Lovable
steps.text: Export the project’s code from Lovable, for example through its GitHub connection, and put it in a folder on your computer.

steps.name: Build it into static files
steps.text: Lovable projects are code, not finished pages, so they need a build first. In the project folder, run npm run build. The output folder (often called dist) is what Aero hosts.

steps.name: Start a new site in Aero
steps.text: Go to Sites, New site, and pick Upload HTML. Give the site a name.

steps.name: Drop in the build folder
steps.text: Drop the build folder, or a zip of it. index.html needs to be at the top. The site is live in seconds.

steps.name: Open the site
steps.text: Aero opens the site’s page: the address, a preview and its versions.

alt.h: Prefer to let a coding agent do it?
alt.p: Open the project in Claude Code, Cursor or Codex, then copy the prompt from New site, From Claude or ChatGPT and paste it there. The prompt tells the agent to build the project, zip the output and send it to Aero. Nothing to install.

gets: A live site at an address like yourname.aeroapp.ai
A static copy of your build. The project in Lovable doesn’t change
Every version kept, so you can go back
On the free plan the site stays live for 7 days
faq: Is there a Lovable integration?
No. Aero doesn’t connect to Lovable. You export the code, build it, and upload the result, or let a coding agent do those steps.
Does my Lovable project change?
No. Aero hosts a copy of the built files. Your project in Lovable stays as it is.
How do I update the site?
Change the project, build it again and upload the new folder to the same site. Aero keeps every version.
Can I keep it private?
Add a password on Basic and up, so only people you give it to can open it.
How long does a free site stay live?
7 days. Paid plans keep it live; they start at $3 a month with a 7-day free trial.

title: Publish a Figma prototype
metaTitle: Publish a Figma prototype at its own address · Aero
description: Turn a Figma prototype link into a site at its own aeroapp.ai address. Share the prototype, paste the link into Aero, and send the address.
answer: Share your prototype in Figma so anyone with the link can view it, then paste its link into Aero. You get a site at its own address that shows the live prototype.
needs: A Figma prototype
The prototype shared so anyone with the link can view it
An Aero account (free)

steps.name: Share the prototype in Figma
steps.text: Back in your Figma file, click Share, choose Anyone and View. Aero checks this for you and tells you if the link can’t be opened yet.

steps.name: Start a new site from Figma
steps.text: In Aero, go to Sites, New site, and pick From Figma.

steps.name: Paste the link
steps.text: Paste your prototype link. If you paste a design or file link instead, Aero turns it into a prototype link and says so.

steps.name: Publish and open the site
steps.text: Aero opens the site’s page with its address and a preview. Send the address to anyone.

alt.h: Want real HTML instead of an embed?
alt.p: Under Other ways on the same screen, Convert with AI lets Claude or ChatGPT read your design and build HTML (it needs a paid Figma seat). Export with a plugin points you to Anima, Figma to Code or pxCode, then you drop the HTML file in.

gets: A site at its own address that shows your live Figma prototype
One link for now. You can add links for other screen sizes later in Settings
On the free plan the site stays live for 7 days
faq: Does the Figma file need to be public?
The prototype needs to be viewable by anyone with the link. Sharing is about access: the link decides which screen opens first.
Does Aero copy my design?
The site shows your live prototype from Figma. Nothing is converted unless you choose Convert with AI or a plugin.
Can I keep it private?
Add a password on Basic and up, so only people you give it to can open it.
How long does a free site stay live?
7 days. Paid plans keep it live; they start at $3 a month with a 7-day free trial.
Can I test it with people?
Yes. Start a new test with the same link and send people the test link.

steps.name: Start a new site

steps.name: Drop in your files

steps.text: Aero puts the site live and opens its page: the address, a preview and its versions.

alt.h: Prefer to let a coding agent do it?
alt.p: Open the project in Claude Code, Cursor or Codex, then copy the prompt from New site, From Claude or ChatGPT and paste it there. The prompt tells the agent to build the project, zip the output and send it to Aero.

gets: A live site at an address like yourname.aeroapp.ai
Every version kept, so you can go back
On the free plan the site stays live for 7 days

The built site, with index.html at the top of the zip rather than inside another folder.

Yes, on Solo and up. Every site also has an aeroapp.ai address, and on Basic and up you choose its name.

How long does a free site stay live?
7 days. Paid plans keep it live; they start at $3 a month with a 7-day free trial.

Yes. Start a new test and pick this site. You get a test link to send to anyone.

title: User test a Figma prototype
metaTitle: User test a Figma prototype with a link · Aero
description: Run a think-aloud test on a Figma prototype. Paste the link into Aero, add tasks, send the test link, and get recordings and summaries back.
answer: Paste your Figma prototype link into a new test in Aero, add a few tasks, and send the test link. Testers talk through it, and you get the recording, transcript and summary back.
needs: A Figma prototype shared so anyone with the link can view it
An Aero account (free)
A few people to send the link to

steps.name: Share the prototype in Figma
steps.text: Click Share, choose Anyone and View. Aero checks this when you paste the link.

steps.name: Start a new test from Figma
steps.text: In Aero, go to Tests, start a new test, and pick From Figma. Paste your prototype link.

steps.name: Add tasks (optional)
steps.text: Write 1 to 5 short tasks, like “Find your cards”. With no tasks, testers explore freely and the review sums up the whole session.

steps.name: Send the test link
steps.text: Copy the test link and send it to your testers. They open it on their own computer and talk through what they do.

steps.name: Review the sessions
steps.text: Each session comes back with the recording, a transcript about a minute after they finish, and a summary.

alt.h: Already published the prototype as a site?
alt.p: Start a new test and pick One of your sites. The test uses that site.

gets: A recording of the tester’s browser tab and their voice
A transcript about a minute after they finish
A summary of each session, with friction points
A test link that works without an account
faq: Do testers need an account?
No. They open the test link and follow the tasks.
Does Aero find testers for me?
No. You send the link to your own people: friends, clients or classmates.
What is recorded?
The tester’s browser tab and their voice. Not their face.
How many sessions do I get?
Free has 3 test sessions. Basic has 5, Solo 10 and Pro 20. Every plan includes transcripts and summaries.
